description: Maximum total weight of a general-graph matching using primal-dual blossom contraction and expansion.

source.title: Weighted Matching
source.reference: Combinatorial Optimization, Algorithms and Combinatorics 21, Chapter 11 (Springer, 2002)
source.algorithm_attribution: Edmonds weighted primal-dual matching with odd-set contraction

input.encoding: [N, M, u0, v0, w0, ...] with one triple per undirected edge
input.edge_rule: simple undirected graph; endpoint order is arbitrary; loops and repeated unordered pairs are invalid

output.encoding: maximum sum of weights of pairwise vertex-disjoint input edges; the empty matching has value zero

workspace.meaning: Fixed dense primal-dual edge, blossom, provenance, and alternating-forest arrays; input storage is supplied by the caller.

contract.objective: maximize total selected edge weight, without a cardinality tiebreaker
contract.method: maintain dual labels, search tight edges in alternating forests, contract odd cycles, adjust labels to expose a tight edge or zero-dual blossom, and expand blossoms when needed
contract.distinction: The sibling general_weighted_matching profile uses subset dynamic programming and is bounded to 16 vertices; this profile uses polynomial weighted blossom through 64 vertices.

complexity.primary_oracle_time: O(2^k * k^2) for fixture components of size k <= 18; hand-derived sparse cases cover larger fixtures
complexity.independent_oracle_time: O(2^M * M) on small fixtures; hand-derived sparse cases cover larger fixtures
